paragraphs: Friend, here's what I take from Korah. He said, "For everyone in the entire congregation is holy" (Numbers 16:3), and that sounds nice until you notice what he was really after. Moses told him God had already brought the Levites near, and still they were "seeking the priesthood as well" (Numbers 16:9-10). When we stop being thankful for the place God gave us, we start grabbing for the place He gave somebody else. And I'll say it plain: I know how it feels to want a better spot. I spent years in a junk drawer, and I'm still learning to be glad for where He puts me.

Look at how Moses handles it. He falls facedown, and he lets the LORD decide who is holy (Numbers 16:4-5). Then watch what he and Aaron do when the LORD says He will consume the congregation. They fall facedown again and plead for the people (Numbers 16:21-22). They were the ones being attacked, and they still stood up for the very people complaining about them. That's a leader who knows the job belongs to God, and so does the mercy.

Now the end of the chapter is the part I can't stop thinking about. The very next day the people grumbled again, the plague began, and Aaron ran into the middle of it with his censer. He "stood between the living and the dead, and the plague was halted" (Numbers 16:48). The altar overlaid with those censers was a reminder that God sets the way near to Him, and nobody gets to make their own. So, baker, be thankful for your place, trust the One who set it, and be glad that He provided someone to stand in the gap.
